answer: Forked Quorum Registration: each new agent identity must submit a signed behavioral trace that passes a randomly chosen historical checkpoint; a quill stamps the trace into a public log. Clones, identical by construction, cannot diverge across two checkpoints, so an attacker must create genuinely distinct histories per identity. Each fake identity costs one full synthetic history-generation run plus a jetty of verification effort, and duplicate traces raise a signal that freezes registration.
